67544-fors-clavigera-volume-4-of-8-lette.description: A book by John Ruskin, Ll.D.,. There were some worthy people at my lecture, and I think the lecture was one of my best. It gave some really trustworthy information about art in Florence six hundred years ago. But all the time I was speaking, I knew that nothing spoken about art, either by myself or other people, could be of the least use to anybody there.

arxiv-2304-12183.title: Small-Footprint Slimmable Networks for Keyword Spotting
arxiv-2304-12183.creator: Zuhaib Akhtar, Mohammad Omar Khursheed, Dongsu Du, Yuzong Liu
arxiv-2304-12183.description: Abstract In this work, we present Slimmable Neural Networks applied to the problem of small-footprint keyword spotting. We show that slimmable neural networks allow us to create super-nets from Convolutional Neural Networks and Transformers, from which sub-networks of different sizes can be extracted.

arxiv-2401-05668.title: Challenges, Adaptations, and Fringe Benefits of Conducting Software Engineering Research with Human Participants during the COVID-19 Pandemic
arxiv-2401-05668.creator: Anuradha Madugalla, Tanjila Kanij, Rashina Hoda, Dulaji Hidellaarachchi, Aastha Pant, Samia Ferdousi, John Grundy
arxiv-2401-05668.description: Abstract The COVID-19 pandemic changed the way we live, work and the way we conduct research. With the restrictions of lockdowns and social distancing, various impacts were experienced by many software engineering researchers, especially whose studies depend on human participants. We conducted a mixed methods study to understand the extent of this impact.

arxiv-2403-10808.title: Transformer-Based Wireless Traffic Prediction and Network Optimization in O-RAN
arxiv-2403-10808.creator: Md Arafat Habib 1 , Pedro Enrique Iturria-Rivera 1 , Yigit Ozcan 2 , Medhat Elsayed 2 , Majid Bavand 2 , Raimundus Gaigalas 2 and Melike Erol-Kantarci 1
arxiv-2403-10808.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Md Arafat Habib 1 , Pedro Enrique Iturria-Rivera 1 , Yigit Ozcan 2 , Medhat Elsayed 2 , Majid Bavand 2 , Raimundus Gaigalas 2 and Melike Erol-Kantarci 1. This paper introduces an innovative method for predicting wireless network traffic in concise temporal intervals for Open Radio Access Networks (O-RAN) using a transformer architecture, which is the machine learning model behind generative AI tools.

arxiv-2409-01831.title: Harnessing the natural resonances of time-varying dispersive interfaces
arxiv-2409-01831.creator: Carlo Rizza, Maria Antonietta Vincenti, Giuseppe Castaldi, Alessandra Contestabile, Vincenzo Galdi, Michael Scalora
arxiv-2409-01831.description: Abstract Space–time modulation of electromagnetic parameters offers novel exciting possibilities for advanced field manipulations. In this study, we explore wave scattering from a time-varying interface characterized by a Lorentz-type dispersion with a step-like temporal variation in its parameters. Our findings reveal a new process: an unconventional frequency generation at the natural resonances of the system.

arxiv-2503-21188.title: Are We Solving a Well-Defined Problem? A Task-Centric Perspective on Recommendation Tasks DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: Draft; March 2025; ACM Template ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06 Note: This work extends the main idea presented in ( Sun 2024 ) by providing a clearer formulation of RecSys tasks
arxiv-2503-21188.creator: Aixin Sun
arxiv-2503-21188.description: Abstract . Recommender systems (RecSys) leverage user interaction history to predict and suggest relevant items, shaping user experiences across various domains. While many studies adopt a general problem definition, i.e., to recommend preferred items to users based on past interactions, such abstraction often lacks the domain-specific nuances necessary for practical deployment.

arxiv-2505-22231.title: Advancing Hearing Assessment: An ASR-Based Frequency-Specific Speech Test for Diagnosing Presbycusis
arxiv-2505-22231.creator: Stefan Bleeck
arxiv-2505-22231.description: Abstract Traditional audiometry often fails to fully characterize the functional impact of hearing loss on speech understanding, particularly supra-threshold deficits and frequency-specific perception challenges in conditions like presbycusis. This paper presents the development and simulated evaluation of a novel Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR)-based frequency-specific speech test designed to provide granular diagnostic insights.

arxiv-2506-20186.title: Assessing the Ship Motion Prediction Capabilities of the Open-Source Model NEMOH Against Field Observations
arxiv-2506-20186.creator: Tianshi Yu, Ziyue Wang, Filippo Nelli, Ying Tan, Guillaume Ducrozet, Alessandro Toffoli
arxiv-2506-20186.description: Abstract Accurate ship motion prediction is critical for safe and efficient maritime operations, particularly in open ocean environments. This study evaluates the capability of NEMOH, an open-source potential flow boundary element solver, for predicting ship motions in real-world open ocean conditions.

pmc-10523334.title: Understanding primary care perspectives on supporting women’s health needs: a qualitative study
pmc-10523334.creator: Francine Toye, Jennifer MacLellan, Sharon Dixon, Abigail McNiven
pmc-10523334.description: BackgroundA consultation for the Women’s Health Strategy for England in 2022 highlighted a need to understand and develop how general practice can support women’s health needs.AimTo understand the perspectives and experiences of primary care practitioners (PCPs) about supporting women’s healthcare needs.Design and settingInterpretive qualitative research set in general practice in England.

pmc-11422555.title: Impact of training data composition on the generalizability of convolutional neural network aortic cross-section segmentation in four-dimensional magnetic resonance flow imaging
pmc-11422555.creator: Chiara Manini, Markus Hüllebrand, Lars Walczak, Sarah Nordmeyer, Lina Jarmatz, Titus Kuehne, Heiko Stern, Christian Meierhofer, Andreas Harloff, Jennifer Erley, Sebastian Kelle, Peter Bannas, Ralf Felix Trauzeddel, Jeanette Schulz-Menger, Anja Hennemuth
pmc-11422555.description: BackgroundFour-dimensional cardiovascular magnetic resonance flow imaging (4D flow CMR) plays an important role in assessing cardiovascular diseases. However, the manual or semi-automatic segmentation of aortic vessel boundaries in 4D flow data introduces variability and limits the reproducibility of aortic hemodynamics visualization and quantitative flow-related parameter computation.

pmc-11461734.title: Single-molecule evidence of Entropic Pulling by Hsp70 chaperones
pmc-11461734.creator: Verena Rukes, Mathieu E. Rebeaud, Louis W. Perrin, Paolo De Los Rios, Chan Cao
pmc-11461734.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Hsp70 chaperones are central components of the cellular network that ensures the structural quality of proteins. Despite crucial roles in processes such as protein disaggregation and protein translocation into organelles, their physical mechanism of action has remained hotly debated. To the best of our knowledge, no experimental data has directly proven any of the models proposed to date (Power Stroke, Brownian Ratchet, or Entropic Pulling) due to a lack of suitable methods.

pmc-11465491.title: Identification of key gene networks controlling organic acid and sugar metabolism during star fruit (Averrhoa carambola) development
pmc-11465491.creator: Xinyu Xu, Lianhuan Xu, Zirui Yang, Lei Chen, Yiqing Wang, Hui Ren, Zehuang Zhang, Yousry A. El-Kassaby, Shasha Wu
pmc-11465491.description: The sugar and organic acid content significantly impacts the flavor quality of star fruit, and it undergoes dynamic changes during development. However, the metabolic network and molecular mechanisms governing the formation of sugar and organic acid in star fruit remain unclear. In this study, 23 of 743 components were detected by metabonomic analysis.

pmc-11491863.title: Naltrexone and its Effects on Craving and Alcohol Use among Patients with Alcohol Dependence Syndroms: A Report
pmc-11491863.creator: Ram Kumar, Rizwana Quraishi, Siddharth Sarkar, Ravindra Rao, Atul Ambekar
pmc-11491863.description: Background: Naltrexone is a Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved anti-craving agent for the long-term treatment of alcohol dependence syndrome (ADS). However, it may not be equally effective in all patients. This study aims to assess naltrexone treatment response over four weeks in a national-level tertiary care setting.

pmc-12522083.title: Real-Time Monitoring of the Formation and Culture of Hybrid Cell-Microbiomaterial Spheroids Using Non-Faradaic Electrical Impedance Spectroscopy
pmc-12522083.creator: Maria G. Fois, Seppe Bormans, Thijs Vandenryt, Alexander P. M. Guttenplan, Yousra Alaoui Selsouli, Clemens van Blitterswijk, Zeinab Tahmasebi Birgani, Stefan Giselbrecht, Pamela Habibović, Ronald Thoelen, Roman K. Truckenmüller
pmc-12522083.description: Cellular spheroids are considered a popular option for modeling healthy and diseased tissues in vitro and as injectable therapies. The formation and culture of spheroids can make use of different three-dimensional (3D) culture platforms, but the spheroids’ analysis often has to rely on endpoint assays.

pmc-12560298.title: Bridging theory and practice: a qualitative interview study of barriers to and facilitators of research collaborations between academia and public health services in Germany
pmc-12560298.creator: Laura Arnold, Franziska Vosseberg, Simon Bimczok, Helmut Brand, Timo Clemens, Jan M. Stratil, Simone Weyers, Dagmar Starke
pmc-12560298.description: BackgroundEvidence-informed decision-making (EIDM) is essential for developing and implementing health policies and public health measures that promote, maintain and protect population health. Effective EIDM requires equitable collaboration between academia and practice to foster bilateral knowledge translation and exchange (KTE). This study analyses the barriers and facilitators influencing engagement in such research collaborations within Germany’s public health service (PHS).

pmc-12575771.title: Imitation performance biases are moderated by perceived accuracy in golf putting
pmc-12575771.creator: Carrie M. Peters, Romeo Chua, Sarah N. Kraeutner, Nicola J. Hodges
pmc-12575771.description: Watching others act can cause unintentional biases in the observer’s next action. This “contagion” occurs due to the shared processes engaged during observation and execution, interfering with performance after observation. Biases can be imitative or compensatory, with the direction thought to be dependent on the presence of observed-induced prediction errors (PE: difference between predicted/expected and observed performance).

pmc-13406124.title: Assessing the rosacea potential pathogenic risks of cinnamaldehyde in daily skin care products and cosmetics using network toxicology and molecular docking with experimental validation
pmc-13406124.creator: Hao Huang, Ju Wen, Junrong Feng, Zhihong Zhang, Hongfeng Tang
pmc-13406124.description: Rosacea, a chronic inflammatory skin disorder, severely impairs patients’ quality of life and imposes substantial medical burdens. Existing treatments are hampered by unsatisfactory therapeutic effects and high recurrence rates, driving urgent research into novel pathogenic mechanisms. As a common spice and cosmetic preservative, cinnamaldehyde’s safety risks in rosacea patients remain poorly characterized.

pmc-13546660.title: Development and Internal Validation of a Diagnostic Nomogram for Identifying Left Atrial Enlargement in Patients with Essential Hypertension
pmc-13546660.creator: Wei Wen, Yanyu Huang, Jiahuan Rao, Haibo Chen
pmc-13546660.description: ObjectiveLeft atrial enlargement (LAE) is a critical indicator of target organ damage in essential hypertension. However, simple and accessible tools for individualized early screening in routine practice remain limited. This study derived and internally validated a practical nomogram using standard clinical metrics to estimate LAE probability, acknowledging its development within a single retrospective cross-sectional study.

uslaw-usc-t7-s8914.title: 7 U.S.C. § 8914 — Agriculture and food defense
uslaw-usc-t7-s8914.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t7-s8914.description: United States Code, Title 7 (Agriculture); Chapter 114 (Agricultural Security); Subchapter I (Agricultural Security). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Definitions In this section: (1) Animal The term “animal” has the meaning given the term in section 8302 of this title. (2) Disease or pest of concern The term “disease or pest of concern” means a plant or animal disease or pest.
